summary.title: Career Decisions
summary.one_liner: A framework from Elad Gil for choosing your next job: weigh network, market growth rate, optionality and brand most heavily, and worry less about exact role and compensation.
keywords: how to pick a startup to join
equity worth nothing at failed company
should i move to silicon valley
takeaways: Optimize most for network: the people you work with and the investors, founders and advisors around the company, since Silicon Valley networks repeatedly work together.
Pick a company in a strong market with good growth; growth creates internal opportunities and signals a good market.
Prioritize optionality, meaning roles that open up new markets or functions later, since people tend to underweight it.
Brand matters most if you lack a name brand on your resume; after 1-2 brands, other factors matter more.
Compensation is the least important factor; equity in a great company can outperform cash or equity at a poor company, and strong companies tend to shift toward paying market cash over time.
summary.summary: This essay by Elad Gil gives a personal framework for deciding which company to join next in one's career, aimed mainly at early-career people joining existing companies rather than starting their own. It lists factors to overweight (network, market and growth rate, optionality, brand) and factors that matter less than people think (exact role and compensation), with examples drawn from companies like PayPal, Google, Facebook and Stripe. It closes with bonus points on moving to Silicon Valley or New York and on international experience, and footnotes note that personal and family circumstances can outweigh the framework. The page also lists many unrelated hiring posts by the author, which are not part of the essay.
